about.title: Ventura Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Public collision records show nine traffic deaths in Ventura in 2025. Each of those numbers was a parent, a partner, a son or daughter — someone whose absence is now felt at a kitchen table somewhere off Telegraph Road or Victoria Avenue. If you are reading this because you lost someone that way, or because a fall, a defective product, or a medical error took them, you are not looking for statistics. California gives certain family members the right to bring a wrongful death claim. Spouses, domestic partners, and children stand first in line; other dependents and heirs may qualify when there is no surviving spouse or child. The claim is civil, separate from anything a prosecutor in Ventura County decides to do, and it generally must be filed within two years of the date of death — sooner if a city, county, or state agency is involved. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is considerably shorter when a public agency is involved. Getting an independent attorney involved sooner keeps those dates from slipping.

items.question: What can a Ventura family actually recover in a wrongful death case?
items.answer: California allows recovery of funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. The specifics depend on your relationship to the person and the circumstances of the death. An attorney can explain how these categories apply to your family without making promises about amounts.

items.question: The driver who hit my husband on Telegraph Road is facing charges. Do I have to wait for that case?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action, entirely separate from anything the Ventura County District Attorney pursues. You can move forward regardless of whether criminal charges are filed, dropped, or result in a conviction. Waiting can actually work against you because the two-year civil deadline keeps running.
